soundness_flags.label: Theorem 1, Theorem 4, tldr, and honest_scope
soundness_flags.one_line: The model class contains only observed-data laws satisfying a mean-Verma equality, but the proposal repeatedly concludes a Napkin intervention-mean/causal interpretation without declaring the required Napkin SCM or potential-outcome identification assumptions.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 4–6, especially pp. 4–5 and equations (1)–(2) on p. 6
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper derives the Napkin ratio-of-g-formulas target, reports exact efficiency for discrete Z and local efficiency for continuous Z, and uses an arbitrary prespecified averaging density for continuous Z.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 13–16, equations (17)–(25) and continuous-index discussion on p. 16
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives the mean-scale orthocomplement and minimum-variance influence-function characterization; for continuous indexing it optimizes within selected finite-dimensional weighting classes and describes richer classes as approximations.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a primitive Napkin causal-model/identification condition—consistency, the relevant ignorability/fixing assumptions, and no direct Z-to-Y effect—or consistently recast every headline claim as observed-law efficiency only.

State explicitly that the global optimizer is outside the finite-dimensional affine classes treated by the 2026 Napkin paper, and add a concise comparison corollary that identifies its finite-family class and strict inclusion.
Make the concentration OEQ’s success criterion a finite-sample theorem with explicit constants and a demonstrated operator-Lipschitz map from joint-moment sup-norm errors to C and L errors.

recommended_next_step: Revise the causal-model scope before Stage 0, then retain the field-tier global-attainment kernel and its primitive concentration obligation.
